# wallix.bastion.certificate_authority

Manage certificate authorities on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a certificate authority on a WALLIX Bastion.
- The Bastion uses certificate authorities to validate the certificates presented by devices or users, as an X.509 CA certificate or an SSH CA public key.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_certificate_authority` Terraform resource.
- Requires API version v3.12 or later.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-ca-certificate"></a>**ca_certificate** | `str` | The CA certificate in PEM format for [`ca_type=X509`](#parameter-ca-type), or the SSH CA public key in OpenSSH format for [`ca_type=SSH`](#parameter-ca-type).<br>Leading and trailing white space and line endings are ignored when comparing with the Bastion.<br>Required when the certificate authority does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state). |
| <a id="parameter-ca-type"></a>**ca_type** | `str` | Type of the certificate authority.<br>Required when the certificate authority does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Choices: `SSH`, `X509` |
| <a id="parameter-certificate-authority-name"></a>**certificate_authority_name** | `str` / required | Name of the certificate authority. Identifies it on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the certificate authority. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the certificate authority should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- [`ca_type`](#parameter-ca-type) and [`ca_certificate`](#parameter-ca-certificate) can be changed in place; change both together.
- The certificate authority is looked up by [`certificate_authority_name`](#parameter-certificate-authority-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Declare the corporate X.509 certificate authority
  wallix.bastion.certificate_authority:
    certificate_authority_name: corp-x509-ca
    ca_type: X509
    ca_certificate: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'certs/corp-ca.pem') }}"
    description: Corporate X.509 certificate authority

- name: Declare an SSH certificate authority
  wallix.bastion.certificate_authority:
    certificate_authority_name: corp-ssh-ca
    ca_type: SSH
    ca_certificate: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'certs/corp-ssh-ca.pub') }}"

- name: Remove a certificate authority
  wallix.bastion.certificate_authority:
    certificate_authority_name: corp-ssh-ca
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-certificate-authority"></a>**certificate_authority** | `dict` | The certificate authority as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected certificate authority. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-certificate-authority) |
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the certificate authority already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["ca_certificate"]` |

### Sample of `certificate_authority`

```yaml
ca_certificate: 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIC8AUFSJcx+fgI7j0JboX1MhgxEot4gYI1sJubI9HsG3
  corp-ssh-ca

  '
ca_type: SSH
certificate_authority_name: corp-ssh-ca
description: ''
id: 1a0f76858e670b54005056b66c8b
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/certificate_authorities/1a0f76858e670b54005056b66c8b
```
